newsitem.title: USA: GOLF-WOODS SCRAMBLES FROM FOUR SHOTS BACK TO WIN IN A PLAYOFF.
newsitem.headline: GOLF-WOODS SCRAMBLES FROM FOUR SHOTS BACK TO WIN IN A PLAYOFF.

text.p: Rookie Tiger Woods came from
four shots off the pace after four rounds to win the $1.65
million Las Vegas Invitational in a playoff against Davis Love
III on Sunday.
Woods, the heralded rookie who turned professional after
becoming the first man to win three consecutive U.S. Amateur
championships, fired an 8-under 64 to get to 27-under par in
the 90-hole event and force a playoff.
He won the playoff by making a par on the first playoff
hole.
"It's kind of like it was after winning the Amateur. I
can't tell you how it feels right now," said Woods, who earned
$297,000 for the win and now has made $437,194 in five events
which puts him 40th on the PGA Tour's money list.
Woods was playing several groups ahead of Love and had to
wait while Love finished his round to see if he would be in a
playoff. Love eagled the par-4 15th when he drove the green
and then sank a putt from 25 feet. That dropped him to
26-under.
Love tied Woods when he birdied the par-5 16th, but missed
opportunities to win it outright on both the 17th and 18th.
On the playoff hole, the players put their tee shots side
by side in the fairway. Woods hit first and stuck his approach
about 15 feet to the right of the pin. Love followed and saw
his 8-iron skip off the green and into a trap.
Love blasted out to within six feet. Woods missed his
birdie putt, but then tapped in for a par. Love then slid the
par putt that would have kept the playoff alive past the hole.
"He's going to be the next great player out here,
obviously," Love said. "We're all going to have to try to beat
him like we're all trying to beat Phil Mickelson now."
Woods was spurred on by a huge gallery that roared every
time he made a shot. He didn't disappoint the crowd, either,
getting off quickly by making a birdie and an eagle on the
first three holes to quickly tie for the lead.
After his eagle-3 on the 492-yard third hole, Woods parred
out until the ninth.
"I made the turn at 4-under, but I knew I'd have to play
well on the back to have a chance," said the 20-year-old
Woods. "When I started, I figured it would take 28-under to
win, and as it turns out, I was right. I just didn't get
there. But when I got that birdie on 11, it fired me up and I
played well from that point on."
Kelly Gibson and Mark Calcavecchia, each shot 65 and
finished tied for third at 26-under 333.
